_meta.description: The canonical Windows Event Log model. Every field name is a value-bearing element or attribute of the actual EVTX <Event> record, lowercased to snake_case — taken from the Windows Event Log schema itself, never from a vendor normalisation (it is 'Computer' and 'EventRecordID' as the log writes them). The container elements that merely group attributes (<Provider>, <TimeCreated>, <Correlation>, <Execution>, <Security>) are flattened out, since a container is not a field. The whole <System> envelope sits flat on winlog.* — channel, computer, event_id, event_record_id, provider_name/provider_guid (<Provider @Name/@Guid>), level, task, opcode, keywords, version, time_created (<TimeCreated @SystemTime>), process_id/thread_id (<Execution @ProcessID/@ThreadID>), activity_id/relative_activity_id (<Correlation @ActivityID/@RelativeActivityID>), user_id (<Security @UserID>). winlog.data is the <EventData> payload: the <Data Name=X>Y pairs as a flattened name→value map (a <UserData> event's fields fold in here too). windowlicker's goevtx submodule and log2timeline's winevtx submodule each map their own native representation onto this one contract — same data, different source shapes, one model.
